en: The Great and Wondrous Vajra Great Amṛta-Kuṇḍalī Jvālāmālinī Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Sūtra,
translated by Dharmakṣema.
Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Tathāgata Vairocana was on the peak of Kukkutapāda Mountain,
ninety *yojana*s above the earth.
Together with ninety *koṭi-nayuta* *gaṅgā-saṃkhyeya* Buddhas of the ten directions, they all assembled at this place.
Thereupon, the Tathāgata, throughout incalculable *koṭi-gaṅgā-saṃkhyeya* kalpas—
Sustained by the merit and wisdom accumulated through the practices cultivated in this realm,
one dwells in the great vajra samādhi within the dharma-realm of empty space,
giving rise to the great vajra jewel-peak pavilion.
It is lofty, without center or periphery,
interspersed with various great and wondrous jewels and clouds of exquisite gems,
and entwined with whirling flowers.
Blazing, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of light rays swirl and reflect one another;
immeasurable jeweled banners are arrayed on all four sides;
and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of various exquisite leaves and flowers are spread about as ornamental adornments.
Thereupon, the Tathāgata entered the Great Samādhi of the Sublime Vajra Great Amṛta Krodha-Muṇḍalin, Blazing with Intense Flames,
which pervades the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm without limit or boundary.
They become a garland of nectar-flames.
Furthermore, throughout as many Buddha-fields and lands as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of worlds,
they universally become garlands of flames for the Buddhas of the ten directions.

Each entered the great samādhi of the infinite hundreds of thousands of revolutions of the Great Wondrous Vajra, the Great Bliss, the Nectar-like Gaṇapati, the Blazing Mass of Flames, and remained there in profound stillness.
At that time, the Tathāgata Bhagavan Vairocana again entered the Great Samādhi of the Blazing Ambrosia Mañjuśrī,
the Great Vajra of the Wondrous Crown that Turns the Wheel and Manifests the Play of Supernatural Powers through a Hundred Thousand Masses of Ambrosial Light.
Pervading the empty space of the three-thousandfold world system and the dharma-realm,
it formed a great eight-spoked wheel of vajra-flames.
At that time, the World-Honored One did not move from this place, remaining within the hub of the wheel.
Furthermore, within each and every spoke,
there appear great eight-colored vajra-flame wheels,
which radiate light throughout the ten directions and are arranged in a clockwise rotation.
Exhausting the upper limit, the middle limit, and the lower limit—
the four boundless limits—
he brings forth the flaming garland of ambrosia.
Each rotated like a wheel-garland of nooses, revolving with sovereign mastery.
Then, the Tathāgata Vairocana entered this samādhi and, from within that concentration,
slightly opened his two eyes.
At that time, the Buddhas of as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in the Gaṅgā rivers of the ten directions were in the sky,
each manifesting the play of supernatural powers and uttering the wondrous lion’s roar.
In unison, they praised the Tathāgata Vairocana with these four lines of sublime gāthās, saying:
*Namo buddhasya mudor vīralokasumate mahājñānaśvaralambisiddhe.* Having spoken this verse, they said:
The Buddhas of the ten directions addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One, what Dharma do you wish to expound today that you manifest such a physical appearance?
Within the Buddha-fields of the past, we [have seen this before]."
"I have never before seen this samādhi.
At that time, the Tathāgata Vairocana,
by means of his vajra body, speech, and mind, [proceeded].
Extending his exquisite golden arms,
he joins the two palms together and bends the two index fingers into the palms.
Pressing the two thumbs together so that they form the shape of a *uṣṇīṣa*, place this great seal before the heart.

From this seal, there arise immeasurable hundreds of thousands of *koṭis* of wondrous great jewel lights of various colors, clouds of various-colored jewels, and flowers with exquisite, variegated petals.
It revolves in the void like a great golden wheel.
Furthermore, from the mudrā, ten koṭis of Gaṅgā-sand of Buddha-fields appear,
each emitting great light that illuminates the ten directions.
They rained down various precious wheels and exquisite jewel flowers,
and produced great parasols, hooks, vajras, wheels, swords, jewels, and conchs;
furthermore, they emitted most wondrous sounds.
They extend across hundreds of thousands of billions of *koṭi* Buddha-fields.
Furthermore, from each individual jewel-wheel, exquisite flower, great parasol, hook, vajra, wheel, sword, conch, and so forth,
there appear as many manifestations as there are atoms within hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayuta* Buddha-fields.
Each produced immeasurable wondrous sounds,
their resonance shaking ten directions across hundreds of billions of worlds.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, the Sun of Universal Radiance...
With the blazing garland of light from his fierce supernatural power,
he whirls his hand nine times clockwise in the sky above his own head in the manner of a noose-loop.
All the Buddhas throughout the entirety of space were gathered and entirely entered into the light.
At that time, the light rotated nine times without ceasing,
manifesting nine *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka-koṭi* Buddha-fields.
Each sat upon a white lotus flower,
surrounding themselves while emitting immeasurable jewel-light.
At that time, the World-Honored One manifested his body in the form of the Universal Gathering of All Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Cakra-Rājas.
Holding a golden wheel with eight spokes, he sits upon a throne supported by seven lions;
his body emits immeasurable hundreds of thousands of rays of light,
and from the crown of his head he projects flames while a parasol swirls above him.
Above, one koṭi of Buddha-bodies appeared, emitting great radiance;
they all turned and sat within the parasol.
Thus it was, World-Honored One.
With the seal, one should further fashion a golden wheel with eight spokes;
within the eight directions of the eight-colored wheel,
there appear eight kinds of flower seats.
Each bearing their original insignia,
they were each surrounded by eight *gaṅgāśa*-koṭis of Buddha-bodies,
each emitting immeasurable flames of light from various jewels.
Returning to the top of the parasol, one koṭi of Buddhas appeared,
emitting great rays of light that circled individually; then,
before the Tathāgata in the eastern direction, within a crimson-colored wheel—
The Buddha-Usnīṣa-Cakravartin, King of Light-Spikes, appears,
holding the seal of the Tathāgata’s usnīṣa and emitting a great mass of light, seated upon a red lotus flower.
To the right of the Tathāgata, within a yellow wheel, [he resides].
The Sarvabuddhoṣṇīṣacakravartin appears,
holding a yellow lotus from which yellow light radiates, seated upon a yellow lotus,
within a white wheel to the right of the Tathāgata.
He appears as the Buddha-Usnīṣa-Cakravartin with the White Parasol,
holding a white parasol and emitting white light, seated upon a great white lotus.
In the right rear corner is a wheel of variegated colors.
He appears as the Victorious Uṣṇīṣa Cakravartin,
holding a sharp sword and emitting light of various skillful colors,
seated upon a multicolored lotus flower within a red wheel behind the Tathāgata.
He appears as the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa-Cakravartin Sarvāvaraṇaviṣkambhin,
holding a red lotus in his hand upon which is a hook;
he emits red light and sits upon a red lotus.
In the blue wheel at the rear corner,
there appears the yellow Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-cakravartin,
holding a trident-vajra from which blue light radiates, seated upon a blue lotus.
To the left of the Tathāgata, within a green wheel,
appears the One-Syllable Supreme Cakravartin King.
He holds an eight-spoked vajra-wheel and emits green flames of light, seated upon a green lotus flower.
In the purple wheel at the left corner before the Tathāgata,
there appears the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa Cakravartin of Boundless Sound,
holding a white conch shell and emitting purple light-flames, seated upon a purple lotus flower.
As above, the Uṣṇīṣas of the Buddhas of the eight directions each emit light of their respective directional colors,
and each is surrounded by eight *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka-koṭi* Buddhas.
Each sits upon a lotus flower colored according to their respective directions.
Each [lotus] encircles a koṭi of buddha-fields above the crown of the head, forming the shape of a parasol.
At that time, the Sarvabuddhōṣṇīṣacakravartin bestowed seats upon the eight directions,
each manifesting the appearance of one of the eight kinds of Buddhōṣṇīṣacakravartins.

Then the World-Honored One further manifested the seven precious treasures— the woman-treasure, the horse-treasure, the treasurer-treasure, the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the wish-fulfilling jewel-treasure, and the military-treasure—
surrounding this great wheel on all four sides.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of summoning,
pervading the entire dharma-realm of empty space.
All are summoned for this purpose:
to establish all sentient beings so that they may swiftly reach the path of unsurpassed bodhi,
and to cause those dwelling in saṃsāra to realize the Buddha-body.
At that time, the koṭis of Buddhas of the ten directions,
having heard the invocation of the Sarvabuddhoṣṇīṣacakravartin,
all manifested supernatural powers within their meditative absorption.
They rained down showers of precious jewels, precious flowers, precious garlands, precious incense, precious lamps, precious silken banners, and so forth,
all arriving together in the Great Vajra Jewel-Peak Pavilion within the Dharmadhātu of space.
Assembled in the midst of the void, they all spoke, saying: "World-Honored One,
why does the Wheel-Turning King not preach the Dharma of the ten characters,
so that all sentient beings may swiftly attain the Buddha-body in this present life?"
At that time, the King who Subsumes All Buddha-Uṣṇīṣas,
hearing these words, did so because he wished to manifest great supernormal powers and majestic authority,
and because he wished to explain the fundamental practices realized by all Buddhas.
It is taught because it is the Dharma practiced by all Buddhas of the past,
the Dharma practiced by all Buddhas of the present,
and the Dharma practiced by all Buddhas of the future.
It is so that good sons and good daughters may,
in this very life, without changing their physical bodies, be able to accomplish the great work of becoming a Buddha;
and for the benefit of all sentient beings, so that they may attain the body of a Buddha.
Then he spoke the ten-syllable mantra of the Sovereign Wheel-King of the Vajra Blazing Radiance Uṣṇīṣa:
*Namo vighnāntakṛtāya | namo bhagavate uṣṇīṣāya | oṃ buddha buddha buddha buddha* ||
dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhātṛ hūṃ traḥ | dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhataḥ hūṃ traḥ | dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama dhama.
3. *Tṛhūṃ* (three times) 4. *Buddha buddha buddha buddha buddha buddha buddha buddha* (four times) 5.
*Nṛhuṃ* (three times) 6. *Buddha buddha buddha buddha buddha buddha buddha buddha* (six times) 7.
*Hruḥ huṃ* (three times) 8. *Buddha buddha* (two times)

DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ 8 BHRŪṂ HŪṂ 9 DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ 10 HŪṂ 10 DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ DHĀ 10. Having recited this mantra, [he said].
The Buddha-fields, numbering as many as the atoms within the buddha-lands throughout the trichiliocosm, shook in six ways.

A rain of various precious flowers, clouds of jewels, celestial wish-fulfilling gems, white fly-whisks, silk canopies, fragrant flowers, lamps, sounds, songs, and hundreds of thousands of kinds of music fell as offerings to the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, all the Buddhas of the ten directions, numbering in the millions,
having heard this teaching, all bowed their heads at his feet in homage and praised the Tathāgata Sarvabuddhoṣṇīṣavijayacakra-rāja.
Recite this secret mantra:
"Blazing with peerless radiance, supreme, wondrous, and majestic,
the sovereign wisdom that can subdue the wheel of birth and death— may it swiftly cause sentient beings to attain perfect enlightenment."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Wheel-Turning King,
further spoke these secret words in response to the ten directions' koṭis of Tathāgatas and others.
I now speak these words of truth for the benefit of sentient beings so that they may attain equal enlightenment;
may the Buddhas of the ten directions swiftly grant their empowerment, causing all those sentient beings to realize what I have spoken.
Having recited this verse, [he said: "May it be so!"
At that time, there were great bodhisattvas from the worlds of the ten directions,
namely, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha,
the Honored One Maitreya Bodhisattva,
and the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva,
Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin Bodhisattva,
and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
At that time, they all assembled before the World-Honored One, the Wheel-Turning King, at the Jewel-Peak Pavilion in the Dharma-realm of Space.
Prostrating with their heads at his feet, they all uttered this eulogy in the form of a mantra:

*Namo sarvajñāya | manohasini | sarvārthasiddhi | nūhasini | yaśaḥsini | prabhavānuka | vandye | samyaktvaniyatipāpakilamariṇi | namo'stu te tārādharakravaratini | namo'stu te.* Having spoken these words, [he continued].
At that time, each of the eight great bodhisattvas manifested a circle of light and appeared as one of the eight great Vajra-vidyārājas by means of the Tathāgata’s wheel.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi...
He manifests as the Vidyārāja Trailokyavijaya-Vajra,
emitting blue light and displaying two fangs in his mouth;
with a laugh of "aṭṭahāsa," he hurls a five-pronged vajra with his right hand.
The eight-syllable heart mantra is spoken as follows:
Oṃ niḥsvabhāva-vajra hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī manifested himself as the Vidyārāja Vajra with six arms, six heads, and six feet.
He emits light of greenish-black color;
with his teeth biting his lower lip and his two eyes and eyebrows staring wide, he holds a sharp sword in his hand and utters this three-syllable heart-mantra: [Mantra]
HŪṂ AḤ HŪṂ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha manifested as the Vidyārāja Mahāhāsya-vajra,
emitting light of an ash-colored black.
His mouth displays a great laughing expression with two fangs protruding upward;
his left hand rests upon a blue staff,
and his right hand grasps a lasso.
He spoke these ten syllables of the Heart Mantra:
Oṃ vajra ṭha haḥ svā hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Honored Bodhisattva Maitreya...
He appears as the Great Wheel Vajra Vidya-rāja,
his entire body yellow in color and emitting great flames;
in his right hand, he holds an eight-spoked vajra wheel.
With his left hand, he holds a single-pronged vajra.
He then utters this six-syllable heart mantra:
Oṃ vajra-kīla hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
Upon the crown of his head appears the Vidyārāja Hayagrīva,
azure in color and emitting red light;
with his right hand raised above his head.
Holding a lotus flower horizontally as if to strike,
with the left hand forming the kamaṇḍalu mudrā,
he recites this ten-syllable heart mantra:
Oṃ harya kṛvā huṃ phaṭ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha manifested as the Vidyārāja Vajra Aparājita.
His entire body is yellow and emits flames of fire;
with his right hand he hurls a vajra,
and with his left hand he forms the threatening mudrā toward his mouth.
He spoke these thirteen syllables of the heart-mantra:
Oṃ hulu hulu caṇḍāli maṅgī sarvahaḥ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin...
He manifests as the Vidyārāja Acala,
his entire body blue in color and emitting flames of fire;
with his right hand, he holds a sword.
Holding the cord with his left hand,
with a single topknot hanging down from the left side,
he spoke this fourteen-syllable heart-mantra, saying:
Oṃ ācalakrodha jñānasattva hūṃ phaṭ. At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva manifested as the Vidyārāja Ākārṣaṇavajra.
With his right hand he grasps a single revolving lid,
and with his left hand he holds a vajra;
his entire body is the color of space, emitting flames of fire.
He spoke this seven-syllable heart-mantra:
Oṃ hrīḥ hūṃ kuru hūṃ bṛhūṃ hūṃ sṛhūṃ hūṃ jṛhūṃ hūṃ ghr̥! At that time, the Buddha of the Eight Vajra-Vidyārājas—
Thereupon, they requested before the Tathāgata to receive his instructions,
saying, "We shall respectfully practice them.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Wheel-Turning King, addressed Vajraprajñā-rāja Buddha and the others, saying:
If there are good men or good women who uphold this ten-syllable heart-mantra,
you all should constantly attend to such persons day and night, never departing from them.
Do not allow them to remain unaccomplished.
Cause all karmic obstacles of the three periods of time to be swiftly extinguished.
Each of you, by means of your supernatural powers and ritual implements, shall shatter their three types of karma and cause them to attain purity.
Regarding the dharmas of the samādhi of contemplative practice,
may you become no different from me in this present life.
I shall now further explain for you the secret single-syllable heart-mantra.
Listen well!
Having uttered this heart-mantra, *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām ārya-akṣobhya*,
Vajrapāṇi and all the other great vidyārājas—
They all paid homage and said:
"On this day, we shall hear this Dharma;
we shall always bear the Buddha’s wheel upon our own bodies."
I pray that the Buddha, out of his great compassion,
will further expound for me the gateway to the cultivation of samādhi,
so that all sentient beings may swiftly realize the Buddha-body.
At that time, the *gaṅgā-saṃkhyeya-koṭi* Buddhas of the ten directions all spoke these words: "Furthermore,
you should proclaim for us the single-syllable heart-seal (*hṛdaya-mudrā*), the *siddhi*, and other such dharmas."
How may all sentient beings swiftly attain the Dharma of the Unsurpassed Way in this very life?
How may they attain the secret dharmas of superior, middling, and inferior accomplishment?
How may they attain the dharmas of supernormal powers?
"How should one cultivate the dharma of samādhi?
We pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion, will extensively bring benefit to all sentient beings.
At that time, the Wheel-Turning King addressed the Buddhas, Vajrapāṇi, and the other Buddhas, saying:
Listen attentively as I shall further explain for you in detail the gateway of cultivating samādhi,
so that you may swiftly realize the fruit of the unsurpassed path in this very life,
abiding within birth and death yet not entering nirvāṇa.
This shall cause you to attain constant mastery over your body.
Son of good family, I shall now first explain for you the fundamental method of the secret mudrā:
join the two hands with palms hollowed and pressed together.
Insert both index fingers into the palms and press them down with both thumbs;
this is called the Heart Seal, the Dharma of the Single Syllable.
When this mudrā is bound,
the Buddhas of the ten directions, numbering in the tens of millions (koṭi),
will swiftly arrive at that place and empower his body, speech, and mind.
One swiftly attains purity;
as if dwelling in the center where neither body nor mind is perceived,
one realizes the station of a Great Being.
Sharing the same rank as all Buddhas, he is the teacher of future Buddhas,
the teacher of present Buddhas,
and the teacher who transmits the teachings to past Buddhas.
If there is a son of good family who practices this dharma,
he should first visualize within his mind the syllable *Aṃ*,
which enters [the heart] and becomes a white great lunar disc.
The measure pervades the entire dharma-realm, extending to its unsurpassed, middle, and lower limits,
forming a great eight-spoked golden wheel.
Furthermore, within each spoke, eight-colored vajra wheels are arranged in a clockwise rotation.
Based on the previous visualization of the body as the Great Self (*mahātman*),
one forms the shape of Cakravartin within the center of the navel wheel.
Thereupon, one binds the Samaya-mudrā of the Heart of All Buddhas of the Sarvārthasiddhi-Uṣṇīṣa.
With both hands, spread the ten fingers apart and place the two palms together;
then, using this mudrā, place the *daśākṣara-mantra* scattered upon the fingertips.
From each individual syllable, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of multicolored jewel-rays radiate forth.
It radiates throughout the Buddha-fields of the ten directions;
its brilliance is so intense that it is peerless throughout the three periods of time.
Then, with the hand of mudrā, rotate it to the right in the manner of a noose-loop.
One rotation corresponds to one Buddha and one wheel;
nine Buddhas correspond to nine wheels, totaling eighty-one billion koṭis of Buddhas.
As described for their physical forms, so it is with their flower pedestals.
Thus, at the time of the primordial wheel-seal (*mudrā*),
one must not allow the radiance of the seal to be interrupted or its flames to fade.
This seal is named "The Seal that Encompasses All Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa-Cakravartins, the Original Samaya that Generates the Boundless Karman of All Buddhas."
Without relying on the gates of ritual protection or making offerings,

one swiftly accomplishes the great samādhi stage of all Buddhas, attaining the Buddha-body that is beyond the range of visual observation for Bodhisattvas of the Ten Stages and unheard of even by their ears.
Even Buddhas of the same class do not see their own bodies,
let alone other bodhisattvas and the like.
If one performs this rite one hundred and eight times, [the result will be attained].
One realizes the Buddha-body.
For those of superior faculties, accomplishment is attained; for those of middling faculties, it will certainly be accomplished if [the mantra] is recited one thousand times.
If one recites it eighteen thousand times,
even those of inferior faculties will certainly attain the great accomplishment (*mahāsiddhi*).
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Wheel-Turning King...
He further addressed the Buddhas of the ten directions, Vajrapāṇi, and the other Buddhas:
"I shall now further explain the method for the wooden seal.
One should carve a vajra-wheel with eight spokes upon a sandalwood block."
In the hub of the wheel, inscribe the syllables *bruṃ hūṃ* (combined).
On the four sides of the wheel, there are flames and mudrās emitting light.
On the back, carve an eight-petaled lotus flower.
Place the Moon Deity upon the flower; the Ācārya says this refers to the "Vom" (伏免). Having formed this mudrā, recite the one-syllable heart-mantra "A" twenty-one times, pronouncing it with urgency.
In a pure place, smear it with *rasanā* (vermilion) and musk.
Seal the heart, forehead, throat, crown of the head, both shoulders, the area below the navel, and the two knees with the mudrās.
Recite the one-syllable mantra.
Recite the single seal of the syllable A ten thousand times;

one will immediately attain supernatural powers to reach the worlds of the Ganges sands in the ten directions, the Land of Wondrous Joy, the Flower Treasury Buddha-fields, the palaces of the nāgas, and the Heaven of No-Thought.
Within all three periods of time, one possesses sovereign mastery according to one's will, free from all obstructions;
none among the bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, and others are able to know or perceive this.
This is called the *siddhi* of the supernatural powers (*abhijñā*).
Furthermore, one cultivates the gate of samādhi by constantly contemplating the syllable *a* within one's own mind,
until it manifests as the form of a Buddha, its magnitude filling all of space and being without limit.
Suddenly becoming pure, one realizes the Buddha-body;
transcending birth and death, one does not transform the physical body but attains the fruit of outflowlessness (*anāsrava*).
One constantly teaches and guides all those of the two vehicles, Buddhas, and all sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
He speaks all *yogas* with sovereign ease, responding to and transforming according to the capacities of beings;
this is called the *siddhi* of the method for cultivating *samādhi*.
Furthermore, O Vajrapāṇi, when that son of noble family desires to achieve accomplishment, [he should proceed as follows].
The Buddhas of the ten directions shall all cast a great eight-spoked wheel upon his head; he must not fear this,
for it is to eliminate the extremely heavy karmic obstacles of the three actions, as well as the cognitive obstacles of attachment to phenomena and conceptual discrimination.
This wheel emerges from that heart and rests beneath those feet.
Mounted upon that Buddha-body, he becomes just like me.
One should always practice this accomplishment with single-minded concentration, never allowing it to be lost.
At that time, the Ganges-sand number of Buddhas, having heard the Dharma,
each praised the World-Honored One Vairocana and scattered various flowers and incense over him.
Having praised him with sublime mantras, they each returned to their own buddha-fields.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi and the other buddhas,
having heard what was said, asked again:
"O Benevolent One, for what kind of person should this dharma bring accomplishment?
At that time, the World-Honored One, Mahāvairocana Tathāgata, said:
"This dharma brings accomplishment for those of upright mind and those free from discriminative thought."
Furthermore, for those who lack knowledge or vision regarding this, they will certainly attain the accomplishment of my body.
At that time, the eight great bodhisattvas of Vajrapāṇi performed this rite before the Buddha.
In a single moment, they became equal to the Buddha.
Then the eight great bodhisattvas, using "Buddha-flowers" to sing praises of the Buddha, desired to return to their own lands.
At that time, the World-Honored One said:
"Although you have attained the Buddha-body, you have not yet repaid the Buddha's kindness.
At that time, the eight great bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha,
saying, "What constitutes repaying the Buddha's kindness?"
The Buddha said, "Once you have all attained Buddhahood, you must extensively deliver sentient beings;
you must not abide in quiescence to enjoy the bliss of solitude for yourselves.
When the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and others heard this teaching, they [responded].
He immediately transformed his body back into that of a bodhisattva and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
The Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"You should use this dharma to extensively deliver sentient beings and cause them to swiftly attain Buddhahood."
Then Vajrapāṇi and the others said:
"If we do not bring this Dharma to those sentient beings who have not yet been delivered and cause them all to attain Buddhahood,
we vow not to realize perfect enlightenment."
Then the World-Honored One again addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Son of good family, I shall further explain for you the single-syllable gateway of the 'Evil-Entry' letter—the heart within the heart, the secret within the secret."
If a son of good family constantly dwells in this gateway of the single syllable,
he will neither arise nor cease within saṃsāra;
without changing his physical body, he shall realize this Dharma.
This single gateway of letters is that wherein all Buddhas of the three periods of the past, the three periods of the present,
and the three periods of the future eternally abide.
It is impossible for anyone to achieve accomplishment apart from this Dharma.
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
Vajrapāṇi beheld the Golden Wheel of the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa; its wheel gradually expanded until it was vast without center or periphery,
its marks and colors both absent, being the quiescent realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, unable to keep pace with what he beheld, praised [the Buddhas] in verse:
"The nature of all Buddhas is boundless; Its wheel-like form is the Dharma-realm (dharmadhātu).
We have realized this Dharma, And shall extensively deliver all sentient beings."
"How shall the World-Honored One enter and abide in the Great Quiescent Samādhi?
We pray that you will appear for our sake; do not fail the vow you originally made.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Wheel-Turning King, having heard the request of Vajrapāṇi and the others, [responded].
Nor does he manifest a physical body.
Within the state of the space-like dharma-realm, there is a voice that says: "Vajrapāṇi!
The nature of all Buddhas is boundless; their form and characteristics are both sovereign."
Both sound and form are truly real;
though they appear as forms, they are devoid of form. They are originally empty and quiescent;
you should always uphold this Dharma to extensively deliver all sentient beings.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi and the eight great bodhisattvas,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
rejoiced, paid homage, and received it with faith, practicing accordingly.
The Great and Wondrous Vajra Great Amṛta-Kuṇḍalī Jvālāmāla-Pradīpta-Buddhoṣṇīṣa Sūtra
